reasoning: Math Academy graded my earlier intended selection b correct and explicitly states that conclusion, but the implication is mathematically invalid. Being above one tangent line does not force concavity throughout a neighborhood. For a counterexample, let t=x-3 and f(x)=-t+t^6(2+\sin(1/t)) when t≠0, with f(3)=0. Its tangent line at 3 is L(x)=-t, and f(x)>L(x) for every t≠0. Nevertheless, f''(x)=-t^2\sin(1/t)-10t^3\cos(1/t)+30t^4\sin(1/t)+60t^4 changes sign arbitrarily close to 3. The function is decreasing nearby, has no local minimum at 3, and has no consistent concavity on either side. Thus none of the listed statements must hold. This resolves the caveat in my earlier response: b is the captured MA key, but is not a necessary mathematical conclusion.
